title: An answer from the person's table comes with its chart, chosen by code and drawn from the result alone
request: The owner's goal: Home helps people who want numbers, BI and reports from their data; H7a answered in words, H7b shows the chart beside them.
spec: Package H7, part b: each answer carries a chart spec chosen by code from the result's shape (one number, a line over periods, bars for one group, a table otherwise), drawn on the page with the page's own chart helpers; every number in it written as the answer writes it; the numbers' table under the chart.
plan: home_chart.spec from the plan and the result; title and headers from the plan.
The answer message carries the spec; home.html draws it.
Check on the real server at desktop and phone width; review adversarially.

decisions.decision: The chart kind is chosen by code from the result's shape, never by a model.
decisions.why: A chart is part of the answer: it must follow from the result, the same every time.

decisions.decision: The chart's title and table headers are built from the plan (operation, column, period), never from a measure's name.
decisions.why: A model may write a measure's name ('Revenue over 1000') that says something the computation does not.

decisions.decision: The server writes every number's text; the page never formats a number itself.
decisions.why: The chart, the table and the sentence must show the same rounded numbers, each traced to the result.

decisions.decision: At most four lines (the page's four series styles); one period point or more lines fall back to bars or a table.
decisions.why: No new colours outside the design kit; a line of one point says nothing.

change: dclab_rnd/home_chart.py (new); dclab_rnd/home_query.py (count cue from the sentence, row count with its assumption said, 'of 2025', note as sentences); dclab_rnd/draft/brief.py ('of 20XX' as a period); dclab_rnd/draft/chat.py (answer only after the table is described; question passed; chart in the answer); agentic/web/src/views/home.html (answerCard); tests/test_home_chart.py, tests/test_home_answer.py.

findings.defect: A model-written measure name reached the chart's table header.
findings.scenario: A plan naming its mean 'Revenue over 1000' showed that header under the chart.
findings.cause: The table's headers were the result's column names.
findings.fix: Headers are built from the plan's operation and column.

findings.defect: The answer came before the table was described.
findings.scenario: On the real server, a draft created and uploaded at once answered 'Mean of monthly_spend by plan' before 'Your data is ready'.
findings.cause: The start turn ran after a fast upload finished and answered from the ready table.
findings.fix: Home answers only after the active table's description was said.

findings.defect: 'How many orders … in each month of 2025' was refused.
findings.scenario: The brief kept 'orders' as the measure and 'all rows' as the period.
findings.cause: The brief's 'how many X' pattern keeps X only; 'of 2025' was not a period form.
findings.fix: A count cue before the measure in the person's sentence makes a count; with no column naming the thing, rows are counted and the answer says each row was taken as one; 'of 20XX' is a period.

findings.defect: A one-point period or many groups drew a useless line.
findings.scenario: A count per year on one year's data drew a line of one point.
findings.fix: A line needs two periods and at most four series; otherwise bars or a table.

findings.defect: A count from 'how many' dropped the rest of the question.
findings.scenario: 'How many orders were refunded per region?' answered the number of rows by region; 'came from Dubai', 'excluding returns' and 'web' vanished the same way.
findings.cause: The brief keeps one word after 'how many'; the new count cue made a row count without reading the rest of the sentence.
findings.fix: A count from the cue is made only when every word of the sentence is held by a brief field or is plain; otherwise Home says what it cannot apply (the model, where configured, may plan it).

findings.defect: 'of 2000' read an amount as a year.
findings.scenario: 'orders with an amount of 2000 or more' became the period 2000-01-01 to 2000-12-31.
findings.fix: 'of 20XX' is a period only at the end of a clause (before punctuation, 'by' or 'per').

findings.defect: A second 'how many' turned a sum into a count, and a quantity was counted as distinct values.
findings.scenario: 'How much amount per region, and how many amounts were refunded?' answered the distinct amounts by region.
findings.cause: The cue matched a prefix anywhere in the sentence; numeric columns were countable.
findings.fix: The cue needs a word end; 'how much' with it is refused; a quantity column is never counted as distinct values.

findings.defect: A condition the brief missed vanished from a sum.
findings.scenario: 'Total amount by region for orders with a value of 2050 or more' answered the total over all orders, saying nothing.
findings.cause: No field held the condition, and nothing compared the sentence with the brief.
findings.fix: Every rules answer names the words of the question no field holds.

findings.defect: An empty group showed as withheld, and number keys were written two ways.
findings.scenario: The group with no store (8,738.61) read 'withheld (too few rows)' in the table; 10001 was '10,001' there and '10001.0' in the sentence.
findings.cause: Keys went through the number formatter.
findings.fix: Keys are written by one function: an empty group '(no value)', a whole number without decimals, in the sentence, the chart and the table.

findings.defect: A period the floor removed was joined over.
findings.scenario: February removed; the line went from January straight to March.
findings.cause: The axis held only the periods present.
findings.fix: The axis is every period from the first to the last; a missing one breaks the line.

findings.defect: A period label went into the SVG unescaped, and the ordering guard had no test.
findings.scenario: Not exploitable today (labels come from the engine), against the escape-everything rule.
findings.cause: The line chart's tick formatter writes raw text.
findings.fix: The label is escaped; a test shows no answer before the table is described.

measurements.name: Home on the H1 dev requests (rules alone)
measurements.gate: no wrong field, no row, no uncited number
measurements.result: Unchanged by the chart: exits 9 of 36, fields 65 right and 0 wrong, rows 0, uncited 0; the 'of 20XX' period form misread no field

measurements.name: The page on the real server
measurements.gate: bar and line answers drawn, no horizontal scroll at 375 px, no page error
measurements.result: A bar answer (mean spend by plan) and a line answer (orders per month of 2025, 2024 rows left out) drawn; 375 px wide with no horizontal scroll
limits: checked by hand in the built-in browser

outcome: A person asking for numbers sees the answer in words and as a chart, both from the same result, with the numbers' table under it.
lessons: Every label beside a number is part of the answer: build it from the computation, not from a name someone chose.
A check on the real server finds order and wording faults a unit test does not.
A rule that answers sooner must also prove it heard the whole sentence: compare the sentence with what was read, and say the rest.
Test the reader and the planner together on whole sentences; a test that hands the planner a clean brief hides what the reader drops.
risks: The count of rows rests on 'each row is one'; the answer says so, and the person can name the column.
